notes: Synthetic adult geriatric primary-care transcripts. Invented clinicians and patients, no real PHI. Gold quotes are copied verbatim out of the transcripts by hand; the harness re-checks that.

cases.title: Hypertension: amlodipine added, home BP diary
lines: Doctor: Papa's blood pressure is still high, so today we alter the plan.
Doctor: Start amlodipine 5 mg every morning, with breakfast.
Doctor: Continue telmisartan 40 mg at night, exactly as before.
Doctor: Never stop the amlodipine on a day when the reading looks normal.
Caregiver: Should he take it before food or after food?
Doctor: Check his blood pressure every evening and write it in the diary.
Nurse: Reduce the salt in his cooking, and avoid pickles and papad.
Doctor: Come back in two weeks and we will review the creatinine and the sugars.
Nurse: Remember to call us if he feels dizzy or faints after a tablet.

cases.title: Type 2 diabetes: metformin timing, insulin started, lows
lines: Doctor: Amma's sugar control has slipped, so we adjust the tablets today.
Doctor: Take the metformin twice a day with dinner, that is 1000mg each time.
Doctor: Increase the metformin to 1000mg, two tablets in the morning and none at night.
Doctor: Inject insulin 10 units at bedtime, in the thigh, and rotate the spot every week.
Nurse: Check the glucose before breakfast and again two hours after food.
Doctor: Add one extra egg to her breakfast every morning, protein matters more than bread.
Doctor: If she feels shaky, give the glucose powder with a little water right away.
Doctor: Do not skip the morning tablet even if she sleeps late, take it with milk instead.
Nurse: Call the clinic the same day if her sugar runs below seventy or she is too sleepy to wake.

cases.title: Heart failure: diuretic, daily weight, fluid limit
lines: Doctor: His neck veins are up and the ankles are swollen, so today we need a stronger diuretic.
Doctor: Take furosemide 40 mg every morning, nothing after midday.
Nurse: Measure his weight every morning before breakfast and write the number in the diary.
Doctor: Restrict fluids to four cups a day, that is about one litre in total.
Doctor: Do not use ibuprofen or any painkiller from the shop for the leg pain.
Doctor: Avoid salt and pickles, they hold water in the body.
Nurse: Make sure to call us the same day if he gains two kilos in two days or needs more pillows at night.
Doctor: No smoking in the house from today, the smoke undoes the medicine.

cases.title: Statin therapy: myalgia watch, repeat lipids, no self-stopping
lines: Doctor: Her cholesterol is well held on the current statin, so we leave the tablet as it is.
Doctor: Continue atorvastatin 20 mg at night for now.
Nurse: Make sure to report any muscle pain, dark urine or new weakness straight away.
Doctor: Get the liver blood test and the lipid panel done in three months, before you come back.
Doctor: Eat less fried food and keep the walking going after dinner.
Doctor: Measure the calf and arm pain and write down which days it stops her moving.
Doctor: Do not start any over-the-counter painkiller without asking us, especially with the statin.
Doctor: Given the aching, some people stop the tablet on their own, and that is the risk we worry about.
